31: /// A memory mapping for a range of virtual addresses in a [`Vmar`].
32: ///
33: /// A `VmMapping` can be bound with a [`Vmo`] which can provide physical pages
34: /// for the mapping. Such mappings are called VMO-backed mappings. Generally, a
35: /// VMO-backed mapping is a file-backed mapping. There are also some exceptions
36: /// where the pages that need to be mapped are not in a file, but the mappings
37: /// are still considered as VMO-backed, e.g.,
38: ///  - Mappings to the vDSO data.
39: ///  - Shared anonymous mappings, where the mapped pages need to be retained and
40: ///    shared with other processes.
41: ///
42: /// Otherwise, the mapping may not be backed by a VMO, in which case it will be
43: /// private and anonymous. Such mappings will map to newly allocated, zeroed
44: /// physical pages.
45: ///
46: /// This type controls the actual mapping in the [`VmSpace`]. It is a linear
47: /// type and cannot be [`Drop`]. To remove a mapping, use [`Self::unmap`].
48: #[derive(Debug)]
49: pub struct VmMapping {
50:     /// The size of mapping, in bytes. The map size can even be larger than the
51:     /// size of VMO. Those pages outside VMO range cannot be read or write.
52:     ///
53:     /// Zero sized mapping is not allowed. So this field is always non-zero.
54:     map_size: NonZeroUsize,
55:     /// The base address relative to the VMAR where the VMO is mapped.
56:     map_to_addr: Vaddr,
57:     /// The mapped memory object. This field specifies what type of memory is
58:     /// mapped and provides access to the underlying memory object (VMO, device
59:     /// memory, or anonymous memory).
60:     ///
61:     /// The start of the virtual address maps to the start of the range
62:     /// specified in the mapped object.
63:     mapped_mem: MappedMemory,
64:     /// The inode of the file that backs the mapping.
65:     ///
66:     /// If the inode is `Some`, it means that the mapping is file-backed.
67:     /// And the `mapped_mem` field must be the page cache of the inode, i.e.
68:     /// [`MappedMemory::Vmo`].
69:     inode: Option<Arc<dyn Inode>>,
70:     /// Whether the mapping is shared.
71:     ///
72:     /// The updates to a shared mapping are visible among processes, or carried
73:     /// through to the underlying file for file-backed shared mappings.
74:     is_shared: bool,
75:     /// Whether the mapping needs to handle surrounding pages when handling
76:     /// page fault.
77:     handle_page_faults_around: bool,
78:     /// The permissions of pages in the mapping.
79:     ///
80:     /// All pages within the same `VmMapping` have the same permissions.
81:     perms: VmPerms,
82: }
83: 
84: impl Interval<Vaddr> for VmMapping {
85:     fn range(&self) -> Range<Vaddr> {
86:         self.map_to_addr..self.map_to_addr + self.map_size.get()
87:     }
88: }

3: /*
4:  * A framework for writing general tests.
5:  *
6:  * A general test typically consists of two parts, the setup part and the
7:  * test part. The setup part contains setup functions that set up the context
8:  * for the subsequent tests to run. The setup functions cannot fail, and if they
9:  * do, execution is aborted because the subsequent tests will not work as
10:  * expected either. The test functions, on the other hand, can fail, and if they
11:  * do, they are reported as test failures.
12:  *
13:  * The framework provides basic utilities for writing general tests:
14:  *
15:  *  - To define a setup function or a test function, FN_SETUP() or FN_TEST() can
16:  * be used. These functions are automatically executed in the order of their
17:  * definition. Note that the order of execution is _not_ related to whether a
18:  * function is a setup function or a test function.
19:  *
20:  *  - Within a setup function, CHECK() can be used to write a setup expression
21:  * that must succeed. If the expression fails, a fatal error will be reported
22:  * and the execution will be aborted.
23:  *
24:  *  - Within a test function, TEST_SUCC() can be used to write a test expression
25:  * that should succeed. If the expression fails, a test failure will be reported
26:  * but the execution will continue.
27:  *
28:  *  - The number of successful and failed tests is tracked. When a test function
29:  * finishes, a summary sentence is printed describing the number of test
30:  * failures. The program will exit with a non-zero code if and only if there is
31:  * at least one test failure.
32:  */
33: 
34: #include <errno.h>
35: #include <stdio.h>
36: #include <stdlib.h>
37: #include <string.h>

39: /** Starts the definition of a setup function. */
40: #define FN_SETUP(name)                                           \
41: 	void setup_##name(void)                                  \
42: 		__attribute__((constructor(__COUNTER__ + 200))); \
43:                                                                  \
44: 	void setup_##name(void)                                  \
45: 	{
46: /** Ends the definition of a setup function. */
47: #define END_SETUP() }
48: 
49: #define __CHECK(func, cond)                                                     \
50: 	errno = 0;                                                              \
51: 	__auto_type _ret = (func);                                              \
52: 	if (!(cond)) {                                                          \
53: 		fprintf(stderr,                                                 \
54: 			"fatal error: %s: `%s` is false after `%s` [got %s]\n", \
55: 			__func__, #cond, #func, strerror(errno));               \
56: 		exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                             \
57: 	}
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Makes a function call and checks its return value is positive.
61:  *
62:  * The execution will be aborted if the check fails.
63:  */
64: #define CHECK(func)                       \
65: 	({                                \
66: 		__CHECK(func, _ret >= 0); \
67: 		_ret;                     \
68: 	})
69: 
70: /**
71:  * Makes a function call and checks its result with the specified condition.
72:  *
73:  * The execution will be aborted if the check fails.
74:  *
75:  * The return value of the function can be accessed with a local variable named
76:  * _ret.
77:  */
78: #define CHECK_WITH(func, cond)       \
79: 	({                           \
80: 		__CHECK(func, cond); \
81: 		_ret;                \
82: 	})
83: 
84: static int __total_failures;
85: 
86: /** Starts the definition of a test function. */
87: #define FN_TEST(name)                                            \
88: 	void test_##name(void)                                   \
89: 		__attribute__((constructor(__COUNTER__ + 200))); \
90:                                                                  \
91: 	void test_##name(void)                                   \
92: 	{                                                        \
93: 		int __tests_passed = 0, __tests_failed = 0;
94: 
95: /** Ends the definition of a test function. */
96: #define END_TEST()                                                        \
97: 	fprintf(stderr, "%s summary: %d tests passed, %d tests failed\n", \
98: 		__func__, __tests_passed, __tests_failed);                \
99: 	__total_failures += __tests_failed;                               \
100: 	}
101: 
102: #define __TEST(func, err, cond)                                                \
103: 	errno = 0;                                                             \
104: 	__auto_type _ret = (func);                                             \
105: 	if (errno != (err)) {                                                  \
106: 		__tests_failed++;                                              \
107: 		fprintf(stderr, "%s: `%s` failed [got %s, but expected %s]\n", \
108: 			__func__, #func, strerror(errno), strerror(err));      \
109: 	} else if (!(cond)) {                                                  \
110: 		__tests_failed++;                                              \
111: 		fprintf(stderr,                                                \
112: 			"%s: `%s` failed [got %s, but `%s` is false]\n",       \
113: 			__func__, #func, strerror(errno), #cond);              \
114: 	} else {                                                               \
115: 		__tests_passed++;                                              \
116: 		fprintf(stderr, "%s: `%s` passed [got %s]\n", __func__, #func, \
117: 			strerror(errno));                                      \
118: 	}
119: 
120: /**
121:  * Makes a function call and checks its result.
122:  *
123:  * A test failure will be reported if the function does not set the specified
124:  * errno or the specified condition does not meet.
125:  *
126:  * The return value of the function can be accessed with a local variable named
127:  * _ret.
128:  */
129: #define TEST(func, err, cond)            \
130: 	({                               \
131: 		__TEST(func, err, cond); \
132: 		_ret;                    \
133: 	})

135:  * Makes a function call and checks whether it succeeds.

137:  * A test failure will be reported if the function sets a non-zero errno.
138:  */
139: #define TEST_SUCC(func) TEST(func, 0, 1)

147: #define TEST_ERRNO(func, err) TEST(func, err, 1)

154:  *
155:  * The return value of the function can be accessed with a local variable named
156:  * _ret.
157:  */
158: #define TEST_RES(func, cond) TEST(func, 0, cond)
